_doc: Written only by node harness/bin/task.mjs. Phases run in order; P0 (ADOPT + STYLE DISCOVERY) waits for the owner by design and needs task.mjs signoff and task.mjs archsignoff before its gate passes. Later phases are added by the planner at the end of P0 (task.mjs phase-add) from the game's real state.

phases.name: Adopt, style discovery and architecture discovery
phases.goal: The harness drives the game (hook contract, verify, baseline perf), the old repo is audited, and the owner has signed off a style with budgets after side by side tests and an architecture after measured option benches.
exit: window.__game implements docs/GAME_HOOKS.md and the hooks_contract scenario passes
verify --quick and verify --all run green on the game as it is
baseline perf measured on this machine and written to harness/verify/perf_budgets.json
harness/design/STYLE_OPTIONS.md compares the candidate styles with test scene shots and measured frame times
the owner signed off one style (task.mjs signoff), STYLE_BIBLE.md and VERIFY.md look rules are written

harness/design/ARCH_OPTIONS.md compares the architecture options with measured benches on this machine, including the map repair layer (harness/design/MAP_REPAIR.md: sources and licences, pipeline, rules, lane-level road model, map inspector, verification, pilot area), and the owner signed off an architecture (task.mjs archsignoff); TECH.md and docs/ARCHITECTURE.md describe the chosen design
the phases after P0 are planned from the game's current state
the owner signed off a game design (task.mjs designsignoff); GAME.md has the fantasy, core loop, pillars, mission list and progression plan

tasks.title: Harness baseline on the scaffold: coordinate contract, drive scenarios, FD0
tasks.desc: The scaffold already has window.__game (src/debug/hooks.ts) and verify --quick was green on 2026-11-10. Lock the baseline and the coordinate rule (owner inbox: correct coordinates from day 1 with tests). (1) Check the hook contract against docs/GAME_HOOKS.md and fix any gap; without ?debug=1 window.__game.debug must not exist (add a unit test or a scenario that opens the page without debug=1). (2) Add src/geo/projection.ts: lat/lon to world metres and back around one named Delhi origin constant (India Gate, 28.612894 N, 77.229446 E), east +X, north -Z, up +Y, accurate to under 0.5 m within 25 km of the origin (local transverse Mercator or ENU; write the choice to decisions.md as provisional until the architecture sign-off). No mirroring, no axis flips. (3) Unit tests: the origin maps to (0,0); Connaught Place central park (28.6315, 77.2167) lands at x -1246 +/- 25, z -2071 +/- 25 (north-west of the origin); Red Fort (28.6562, 77.2410) lands at x +1129 +/- 25, z -4821 +/- 25 (north-north-east); round trip error under 0.01 m; a point due north has x 0 and negative z. (4) Scenarios (input only, wait in sim time): drive_north (throttle 3 s from heading 0: z falls by over 10 m, abs x under 0.5 m), drive_turn_right (throttle plus steer right: heading grows and x becomes positive), coords_north_marker (camera at the origin looking north shows the red north post in the centre third of the shot; the builder reads the shot). (5) Play script harness/verify/milestones/FD0.js per milestones.json FD0 (real inputs only). (6) quick.json: core = boot_title, hooks_contract, perf_baseline, drive_north; areas mapped to src/car.ts, src/geo/, src/debug/. Notes: this is tooling and tests, no look change.
accept: npm run typecheck and npm test pass; the projection tests named above exist and pass (CP and Red Fort within 25 m of the given x and z, round trip under 0.01 m)

node harness/bin/verify.mjs --only hooks_contract,boot_title,drive_north,drive_turn_right,coords_north_marker passes with no console errors, and the builder read coords_north_marker.png (red post centred, ahead)
node harness/bin/verify.mjs --milestone FD0 passes
a check proves window.__game.debug is undefined when the page opens without ?debug=1
node harness/bin/verify.mjs --quick passes and node harness/bin/verify.mjs --all passes (or each failure is listed as a known bug task)
decisions.md has the provisional projection entry; TECH.md 'Coordinates' names src/geo/projection.ts and its tests
tasks.summary: Transverse Mercator projection around India Gate, no flips; CP and Red Fort land within 25 m; drive_north, drive_turn_right, coords_north_marker, hooks_no_debug scenarios and FD0 pass; quick 7/7. verify --all deferred to the P0 gate (low usage mode).

tasks.title: Tooling: game design sign-off in task.mjs, gates, status and dashboard
tasks.desc: Owner direction 2026-11-10 (inbox mmwap8jxg): Phase 0 needs a third sign-off, the game design. Small tooling task, same pattern as signoff and archsignoff in harness/bin/task.mjs. (1) Add task.mjs designsignoff "<the owner's exact words>": writes designSignoff {at, quote} to harness/state/state.json and a decisions.md entry with the quote, journal line. (2) P0 gets designSignoff: true (through task.mjs, for example a small migration or a phase flag command; backlog.json is written only by task.mjs) and its exit list gains 'the owner signed off a game design (task.mjs designsignoff); GAME.md has the fantasy, core loop, pillars, mission list and progression plan'. CLAUDE.md Phase 0 mentions the game design discovery and the third sign-off

tasks.title: Salvage and quality audit of the old game (read only)
tasks.desc: Owner inbox part 1: a SALVAGE AUDIT of /Users/apple/Desktop/code/delhi-drive, read only (never edit, build, install, run npm or write there). Write harness/design/SALVAGE_AUDIT.md: one table row per item with verdict KEEP (copy after a check), REWRITE (keep the idea, new code), DROP, with evidence (file:line, numbers) and the reason. Cover: data sources and their licences (OSM PBF, Copernicus GLO-30 and why a surface model makes roads float or sink), bake knowledge in backend/worldBuilder/buildRegion.js (projection, tiling at zoom 16, 500 m tiles, binary format, what it did right and wrong), car tuning numbers and the handling model, the 580 frontend tests (read for intent: which checks are worth rewriting as tests here), assets in art-src and frontend/public (quality, licence, Delhi relevance: paan stains, political posters, textures), the lessons in README, TECHNICAL_DOCUMENTATION.md, docs/, TODO.md and CLAUDE.md, and the root cause of each base-layer failure: the mirror axis (worldGroup.scale.x = -1 and negated physics px), overlapping road meshes, misplaced railings, junctions that do not join, terrain and road misfit, tileManager.js at 2346 lines, the leftover cannon-es layer, the 11 GB JSON tiles. End with 'What Dilli Darshan must do differently' (one line each, feeds ARCH_OPTIONS). Then write harness/design/QUALITY_AUDIT.md from harness/design/templates/QUALITY_AUDIT.template.md, 'why it felt thin', scored against a polish and richness bar for a Delhi driving game (visuals, feel: handling, speed sense, camera, FOV, shake; audio: engine, horns, ambience; VFX: dust, smoke, skid marks, heat haze; traffic and life; UI and HUD; performance), every finding with evidence from the old game and a fix size, plus 'What to protect' (the good parts). Evidence for shots: if the already built frontend/dist can be served read only by a static server started from THIS repo (for example the harness static server pointed at that folder) without writing into the old repo, take a few shots and read them; if it needs its backend or fails, rely on code, docs and art files and say so. The owner reads both docs before the style interview, so put a 10 line summary at the top of each.
accept: harness/design/SALVAGE_AUDIT.md exists with a 10 line summary, the KEEP / REWRITE / DROP table (every row has file:line or a measured number as evidence) and the root cause section for each base-layer failure named in the desc
harness/design/QUALITY_AUDIT.md exists, follows the template headings, scores every area, and every finding has evidence and a fix size
git status shows no change under /Users/apple/Desktop/code/delhi-drive (cd there and run git status --short: empty or unchanged from before)
decisions.md has one entry per KEEP item that will be copied, with the reason (CLAUDE.md 'Copy from the old repo only after checking')

tasks.title: Game design options draft (GAME_DESIGN_DISCOVERY)
tasks.desc: Mode GAME_DESIGN_DISCOVERY (owner direction 2026-11-10, inbox mmwap8jxg: a car driving around Delhi is a tech demo, not a game). Write harness/design/GAME_DESIGN_OPTIONS.md with comparison tables and small text sketches (loop diagrams, a sample mission beat sheet, a HUD sketch) covering his 7 points: 1. fantasy options (new auto driver, delivery rider, cabbie who knows every gali, tourist guide, street racer, a mix), one sentence each plus why it fits Delhi; 2. the core loop at 30 s, 5 min and 1 h per fantasy, and the tension sources (traffic, time, money, rivals, police, weather, fares); 3. a big list (40 or more) of Delhi missions and activities (fares, deliveries, races, chases, festivals, wedding baraat routes, monsoon floods, rush hour, night runs, sightseeing tours past real landmarks, side jobs, collectibles) ranked by fun, uniqueness, build effort and map reuse; 4. progression and reasons to return (money, vehicle unlocks and upgrades, reputation by area, unlocking parts of the city, daily and weekly jobs, story or characters, personal bests and leaderboards, photo spots), each marked healthy or chore with the reason; 5. game feel (speed sense, near misses, horn culture, weaving through traffic, drifts, landmarks as rewards) and 3 candidate sets of feel pillars; 6. honest scope: the smallest first playable loop that is already fun in the pilot area (Connaught Place, ITO and Pragati Maidan, Chandni Chowk, one metro line), then what grows from it, each option with fun, cost, risk and needs from the map, AI traffic and art; 7. references (known open world and driving games): what fits, what to avoid; inspiration, never copy. Use the old game's modes (dash, taxi, delivery, free, police, see SALVAGE_AUDIT.md) as evidence of what was tried. End with a recommendation and at most 6 short, clear questions for round 1, each with options. Never invent the owner's answers.
accept: harness/design/GAME_DESIGN_OPTIONS.md exists with one section per point 1 to 7, a comparison table in each of 1, 2, 3, 4 and 6, at least 40 ranked missions and activities, and at least 2 sketches
a recommendation and at most 6 round 1 questions with options are at the end
tasks.summary: GAME_DESIGN_OPTIONS.md: 7 sections, tables, 46 ranked missions, 3 sketches, recommendation and 6 round 1 questions. Self-checked.

tasks.title: Interview sitting 1: style, place and game design round 1
tasks.desc: The main session asks Anmol in short, clear rounds (AskUserQuestion if available, else plain questions) and waits. First show him the 10 line summaries of SALVAGE_AUDIT.md and QUALITY_AUDIT.md. Then follow harness/design/templates/STYLE_INTERVIEW.md rounds 1 (references and mood), 2 (concrete axes) and 2b (the place: Delhi landmarks, road types, signage and scripts, vehicles, street life, weather, light and time of day, materials). In the same sitting run game design round 1: show the GAME_DESIGN_OPTIONS.md tables and sketches briefly and ask its round 1 questions (fantasy, core loop, first playable loop). Also ask the GAME.md 'As found' open questions (what the player does besides free drive, vehicles, day and night, traffic density, target hardware and browsers, size of the first playable area) and his first architecture preferences: is WebGPU-only acceptable or must WebGL2 work, how much disk the source data may use on this machine, is an offline bake on this machine fine. Record every answer verbatim with task.mjs inbox-add "<his words>" --source interview and ack it. Never invent an answer: a skipped question goes to the next round. Delhi world layers (harness/design/DELHI_WORLD.md, inbox mmwapw3co): show its 10 line summary, then ask (short, with options): (a) which landmarks matter most to you, which 2 or 3 are pilot heroes (proposal: Red Fort, Jama Masjid, CP inner circle or India Gate), and which others must be heroes later; (b) which areas to do first after the pilot (CP, ITO, Chandni Chowk are the pilot); (c) which metro line for the pilot (proposal: the elevated Blue Line stretch at Pragati Maidan and Indraprastha). Also ask the salvage audit's open questions (SALVAGE_AUDIT.md section 7): will the game be public or commercial (this decides FABDEM, believed CC BY-NC-SA, unverified); are invented parties and candidates fine on posters; is Euro Truck Simulator 2 still the quality reference; is a top speed near 110 km/h right for Delhi. Skipped questions go to P0-014.

the answers on hero landmarks, area order, pilot metro line, public or commercial, posters, ETS2 and top speed are recorded verbatim, or listed as skipped and carried to P0-014
the DELHI_WORLD.md answers are passed to the planner for P0-006 and noted for P0-018 (public or commercial decides the DEM licence check)

tasks.title: Style options draft, city brief and game design options update (Godot, three characters)
tasks.desc: Mode STYLE_DISCOVERY plus a game design update, after interview sitting 1 (answers in the inbox with source interview; decisions.md 'Game direction from interview round 1' and 'Engine Godot 4, and a compressed Delhi map'). STYLE: Anmol saw a style board artifact with four looks: realistic, stylised realistic (recommended), comic, gritty. His pick is pending (asked in sitting 2). He does not want: cartoony or childish, a generic Western city, a low-poly mobile game. He wants real conditions, poverty included, shown honestly. The engine is Godot 4 on desktop. Write harness/design/STYLE_OPTIONS.md from templates/STYLE_OPTIONS.template.md with those four as the candidates (plus any he named): reference board, the comparison table, and for each candidate a Godot style id used as the user arg --style=<id> (style tests run in Godot, not ?style= in a browser). Performance estimates are for Godot 4.7 Forward+ on this Mac (sun and shadows, SSAO, SSIL, GI choice: baked lightmaps, SDFGI or VoxelGI, volumetric fog, glow, tonemap, draw calls, video memory), with the Mobile renderer noted where it matters. Asset pipeline (AI image and 3D tools, procedural, what Godot imports), AI prompt fit, tooling, risk, scope. The fidelity levels for a city look with honest costs at driving speed and on foot. On-foot views matter now: each candidate says how people, the three characters and street detail at 1.7 m eye height look, and how guns and fights read in it. Name batch A (the two Anmol is most likely to pick: stylised realistic plus one) and batch B. Write the style questions for sitting 2 (which look, which 2 or 3 go into the Godot style tests). Write harness/design/CITY_BRIEF.md from its template with the sitting 1 answers, unconfirmed items marked. Delhi world layers (DELHI_WORLD.md): add a section 'Landmark tiers and area kits per candidate' to STYLE_OPTIONS.md: for each candidate, how a hero, a signature and a marker landmark look and two contrasting area kits (proposal: Chandni Chowk old city bazaar vs Lutyens bungalow road), the asset volume per tier (hero models, signature textures, kit atlases, who makes them), and AI prompt fit for landmark models and kit textures. Put the landmark and area answers from P0-005 into CITY_BRIEF.md (Landmarks table with tiers) and update DELHI_WORLD.md section 9. GAME DESIGN: update harness/design/GAME_DESIGN_OPTIONS.md for the new direction: three playable characters (auto driver, cop, small-time fixer) with their own lives and stories and missions that merge; guns and fights in an over-the-top action movie tone; on foot anywhere; the earlier picks (auto driver only, 'the city is the game', grounded arcade) are to be rethought. Give: 2 or 3 structure options for three characters (switching, story arcs, how missions merge), the core loop at 30 s, 5 min and 1 h per character, 3 candidate pillar sets, combat and on-foot scope options with honest cost (animation, AI, crowds, cover, weapons, police response), how driving stays central, the respect rule applied to crime, police and poverty (honest, never spectacle or a joke; no real parties or real people), a first playable slice (one mission per character plus one merged mission in the pilot districts), scope and risk. Write the game design round 2 questions (at most 6, short, with options), including the two round 1 questions not asked yet: reasons to return, and how police work. The composite map questions are not yours here (P0-028 writes them). Never invent the owner's answers.

tasks.title: Delhi street stand-in scene and perf baseline (Godot)
tasks.desc: The Godot scaffold is a box on a plane, too empty to compare styles or measure anything. In the Godot project add a procedural stand-in Delhi street built by a GDScript builder (for example game/scenes/standin/), reusable by style tests and benches, loaded with debug.load('street') or --scene=street; the default boot is unchanged. From CITY_BRIEF.md: about 300 m of a 6 lane arterial with a median and kerbs, a service lane, one signal junction, a stub flyover ramp (a simple stand-in, not the lane model), footpaths, 40 to 80 box buildings with shopfront bands and sign boards, trees, street lights, a bus stop, 15 to 25 static vehicles (car, auto-rickshaw, bus stand-ins), 20 to 40 people stand-ins (capsules or simple mannequins), and one third-person character stand-in for on-foot views. Landmarks and areas, loaded with 'landmarks' and 'areas' (or placed along the street): one stand-in per tier (hero: an India Gate like arch from a small parts kit; signature: a domed tomb on a plinth or a CP style colonnade block; marker: an extruded footprint with an area material), each with its surroundings (lawn, wall, gate, parking), and two contrasting area kit blocks of about 100 m each (old city bazaar strip: tight shop houses, wires, signs, vendors; Lutyens bungalow road: walls, trees, low white bungalows). Then write harness/look_proof/poses.json with 9 views (car close-up, street at driving eye height, junction, flyover ramp, HUD over play, busiest view from 40 m up, landmark tiers from the road at player height, the two area blocks from 30 m up, on foot at 1.7 m eye height in the bazaar strip; sim held, same moment every run), run node harness/bin/lookproof.mjs --set baseline --perf, read the shots, and write draft budgets in harness/verify/perf_budgets.json (status stays draft) from the measured numbers with headroom, with the target filled in (machine, Godot version, renderer, GPU, resolution, load). Pure stand-ins, no assets needed.
accept: node harness/bin/lookproof.mjs --check passes and --set baseline --perf writes all 9 views and harness/look_proof/baseline/perf.json; the report quotes the machine, Godot version, renderer, GPU and load

the builder read the baseline shots (downscaled): no blank or black frames; the street reads as a Delhi arterial (median, kerbs, shops, vehicles, people); the three landmark tiers differ in detail; the two area blocks look different; the on-foot view is at eye height
perf_budgets.json has draft numbers derived from the baseline with the target text filled in

tasks.title: Architecture options draft for Godot and the composite map (with map repair, lane model and map inspector)
tasks.desc: Mode ARCH_DISCOVERY, now for Godot 4.7 on desktop (Mac and Windows; a web demo maybe later) and the composite map. Write harness/design/ARCH_OPTIONS.md from templates/ARCH_OPTIONS.template.md, using SALVAGE_AUDIT.md 'What Dilli Darshan must do differently', the Godot baseline perf numbers (P0-009), the style candidates, the owner's answers from sittings 1 and 2 (three characters, guns and fights, on foot anywhere, the composite map districts and layout), and the leading game design options. Decisions, 2 to 4 options each, every number marked estimate or measured: renderer (Forward+ vs Mobile; lighting at city scale: baked lightmaps vs SDFGI vs VoxelGI vs no GI with tuned ambient); physics (Jolt vs Godot Physics; VehicleBody3D vs a custom raycast vehicle; CharacterBody3D for on foot; collider shapes per tile: concave trimesh vs HeightMapShape3D plus road meshes); language (GDScript vs C#, which blocks the web export and needs the .NET build and a dotnet SDK, vs GDExtension in C++ or Rust for heavy runtime code); the offline bake pipeline outside Godot (Node reusing tools/geo/projection.ts, vs Python) and what Godot reads (custom binary tiles parsed in GDScript or GDExtension, Godot resources written by a headless Godot import step, or glTF per tile); coordinates (district frames: a transverse Mercator origin per district plus a translation offset, MAP_REPAIR.md 'District frames and stitching'; float precision at the planned map size: 32-bit floats, a floating origin, or a double precision build); the composite map (district selection file, clip and offset, stitching, connector authoring format and tools, filler between districts, the layout options from DELHI_WORLD.md section 0 with the owner's answers); tile streaming and memory (ResourceLoader threaded loads or WorkerThreadPool, tile size, unload, memory per tile); instancing and LOD (MultiMesh, visibility ranges and HLOD, impostors, occlusion culling); textures (VRAM compression on Mac and Windows, atlases); navigation (navmesh baked per tile offline vs at load; agents for pedestrians, police and traffic); animation and crowds (AnimationTree with skinned characters vs vertex animation in MultiMesh for far crowds, LOD); combat runtime (hitscan, projectiles, ragdolls); traffic AI on the lane model; the map repair layer (refine MAP_REPAIR.md: sources with licence, attribution and quality checks, the pipeline with district selection and stitching, rule engine, auto-repair log, per-tile overrides, elevation solver, verification, pilot districts); the lane-level road model; the road graph to junction mesh builder; terrain that conforms to roads; the map inspector (a web page reading baked data vs a Godot tool scene or editor plugin: fly-to, proposed fixes as 3D preview lines with confidence and reasoning, writes per-tile overrides and the inbox, lane widths and splits, area and landmark views); the verify harness on Godot (the debug server and driver from P0-025 to P0-027: keep or change); export and packaging (Mac signing and notarising, Windows build); budgets per system. It listens on 127.0.0.1 (port from --debug-port, default from kit.config.json godot.debugPort) over WebSocket or TCP with JSON messages, one request id per call. (2) Methods: every required hook (state, clock, frames, input, perf, load, teleport, setCamera, timeScale, hold, events, hud) plus shot(path) (viewport image saved as PNG after the frame is drawn), quit, and quality if cheap. Snapshot push: after every drawn frame the server sends a small snapshot (state, clock, hold, the newest events) so the harness can answer the synchronous hooks (state, clock, hold, events) from the latest snapshot; frames, perf, load and shot are request and response. (3) Sim clock with time scale and the sim hold, read by every game system that steps (the car now; later physics, AI and missions), with a fixed physics tick. (4) perf(ms): cpuMs and gpuMs p50, p95 and max per frame (RenderingServer viewport measured CPU and GPU render times plus process time), p95FrameMs, avgFps, drawCalls and triangles (RenderingServer total draw calls and primitives in frame), gpuMB (video memory used). (5) CLI user args replace the page params: --debug, --verify (hides every debug overlay), --quality=<preset>, --style=<name>, --scene=<id>, --arch=<name>, --lockstep, --mute, --resolution handled by Godot itself. (6) Without --debug: no port opens, the debug node does not exist, the game plays the same. (7) Errors: expected situations never call push_error; unexpected ones are also sent as an 'error' event. (8) docs/GAME_HOOKS.md: add a 'Godot transport' section (args, message format, snapshot vs request, shot) and mark the browser params as the web demo path (later). Add game/debug/ to shared_paths.json.
accept: a node smoke script (harness/bin/godotsmoke.mjs or similar) launches the pinned Godot windowed with --debug, calls every required hook plus shot and quit, prints each result, and the builder ran it: every hook answers in the documented shape
the shot PNG from the smoke run exists and the builder read it (downscaled): the scaffold scene, no debug overlay with --verify
a headless Godot test or a smoke check proves that without --debug no port is listening and the debug autoload is absent
hold({at}) pauses the sim within one physics tick of the asked time, and a held sim does not move for 0.2 s of wall time (checked in the smoke script)
docs/GAME_HOOKS.md has the 'Godot transport' section; npm test passes

It launches the pinned Godot windowed at a fixed resolution with --debug --verify and the scenario's args, connects to the debug server, and runs the page-side scripts (harness/verify/scripts/*.js, milestone play scripts, the __sim lib) in a node vm with a window shim: window.__game.ready and version, window.__game.debug where state, clock, hold and events read the latest pushed snapshot and frames, perf, load and shot are remote calls. (3) A console error is any ERROR or SCRIPT ERROR line in Godot's output or an 'error' event. (4) Scenario field 'headless: true' runs Godot headless for script-only checks with no shot or perf (headless has no rendering). (5) Port the scenarios to the Godot scaffold: boot_title, hooks_contract, hooks_no_debug (launch without --debug and prove no port answers), perf_baseline, drive_north, drive_turn_right, coords_north_marker, and the FD0 play script.
